title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 115
text:
8. If, on the occasion of being charged with or informed they may be
prosecuted for any offence, the person asks to make a statement
which relates to any such offence they shall before starting be
asked to sign, or make their mark to, the following:
(a) unless the restriction on drawing adverse inferences from
silence applied, see Annex C, when they were so charged
or informed they may be prosecuted:
 78
‘I, ............................, wish to make a statement. I
want someone to write down what I say. I understand that
I do not have to say anything but if I do not mention
something which I later rely on in court it may harm my
defence. This statement may be given in evidence.’
(b) if the restriction on drawing adverse inferences from
silence applied when they were so charged or informed
they may be prosecuted:
‘I, ............................, wish to make a statement. I
want someone to write down what I say. I understand that
I do not have to say anything. This statement may be given
in evidence.’
